drawing_spec.visual_spec: The core tetrahedral primitive every other optical drawing is built from. Draw the stereocentre as an explicit serif capital letter 'C' at the origin (NOT a bare vertex, per NJC/Ember/YIJC 3-D acyclic drawings). Attach EXACTLY four bonds in a fixed 2-plain + 1-wedge + 1-dash split, arranged so the WEDGE and DASH sit on the SAME side (both left OR both right), one pointing up-ish and one down-ish, while the two PLAIN bonds fan to the top and to the opposite lower side. Canonical left-handed template (butan-2-ol, NJC p7): bond1 plain straight UP ~90 deg to the first/largest chain group; bond2 plain DOWN-RIGHT ~-55 deg to the second chain group; bond3 HASHED DASH UP-LEFT ~135 deg to the smallest group (usually H); bond4 BOLD WEDGE DOWN-LEFT ~-125 deg to the heteroatom/functional group. All four bonds 90-120 deg apart. Wedge = solid filled black triangle, apex (narrow) AT the C, base (wide) at the substituent label = points OUT of plane toward viewer. Dash = 4-6 short parallel strokes perpendicular to the bond axis, growing longer outward, narrow at C = points INTO plane away from viewer. NEVER two wedges, never two dashes, never a wedge or dash drawn horizontal, never the two plain bonds collinear at 180 deg. Substituent groups are condensed text labels (CH3, CH2CH3, OH written HO on a left bond / OH on a right bond, CO2H, Br, H). Optionally mark the C with a small superscript asterisk (*) = 9729 chiral-centre convention.
sources: NJC Isomerism Lecture Notes (Student).pdf p7 (butan-2-ol), p9
Ember EMBER ISOMERISM.pdf notes p7
NJC 10 Introduction to Organic Chemistry.pdf p5 (lactic acid, 2 plain + 1 wedge + 1 dash, wedge+dash open to one side)
NJC 13 Alkene 2022.pdf p12 (2-bromobutane)

drawing_spec.topic: Optical enantiomer pair with a vertical mirror-plane line
drawing_spec.visual_spec: Two complete flying-wedge structures placed side by side, related by a LEFT-RIGHT reflection, with a single thin VERTICAL DASHED/DOTTED line drawn in the gap exactly midway between them = the mirror plane. Label 'mirror plane' (serif) centred above the dashed line; caption the whole pair 'enantiomers' or 'non-superimposable mirror images' below. The right structure is the exact reflection of the left: groups lying on the vertical axis (e.g. the top chain group) stay in place; the wedge/dash pair and side plain bond swap to the opposite side. Reflection preserves bond TYPE (a wedge stays a wedge, a dash stays a dash) but flips its x-position; equivalently the enantiomer may be generated by swapping wedge<->dash while keeping positions (do ONE of these, not both). Central atom is a letter 'C' in both; each may carry an asterisk. Do NOT print R/S, (+)/(-), or D/L on the structures (all out of 9729 scope). An alternative arrow form (no mirror line) uses a horizontal double-headed arrow labelled 'Enantiomers' between the two structures — use the dashed mirror line as the default.
sources: NJC Isomerism Lecture Notes (Student).pdf p7 (butan-2-ol 'mirror plane' + 'enantiomers / non-superimposable mirror images')

drawing_spec.visual_spec: Draw the C=C HORIZONTAL at the centre with BOTH alkene carbons as explicit letter 'C' glyphs joined by a double bond = two short parallel horizontal lines (C=C). From EACH sp2 carbon draw two plain single bonds splayed at ~120 deg (one up-and-out, one down-and-out), giving four substituent slots: up-left, down-left (off the left C) and up-right, down-right (off the right C). ALL four substituent bonds are plain thin lines — NO wedge/dash on an alkene (the unit is planar). Placement rule: cis = the two identical/reference groups on the SAME side (both up-left AND up-right, i.e. both top); trans = the reference groups on DIAGONALLY OPPOSITE corners (up-left AND down-right). Label with the italic word 'cis' or 'trans' centred directly below each structure (or as a name prefix, e.g. 'cis-1,2-dichloroethene'). NEVER use E/Z (explicitly out of the H2 syllabus). Only draw the pair when each alkene carbon carries two DIFFERENT groups; if one carbon bears two identical groups, cis/trans does not exist. Optional polarity overlay: crossed-tail dipole arrows along each polar bond toward the electronegative atom plus a resultant arrow, captioned 'polar molecule' (cis) / 'non-polar molecule' (trans).

drawing_spec.topic: Multiple stereocentres — horizontal two-carbon flying-wedge backbone (2^n)
drawing_spec.visual_spec: For adjacent stereocentres draw the main chain C-C as a HORIZONTAL plain bond joining two letter 'C' glyphs (each optionally asterisked). On EACH carbon: draw the H straight UP on a plain bond (the two H's form a shallow inverted-V peak); the remaining two substituents go BELOW the carbon as one HASHED DASH pointing diagonally OUTWARD to the side and one BOLD WEDGE pointing roughly DOWN. Which of the two lower groups is wedge vs dash encodes each distinct stereoisomer. Lay the full set out either as a 2x2 grid (Isomers A/B/C/D) or as enantiomer pairs each joined by a horizontal double-headed arrow captioned 'Enantiomers'. Annotate the maximum count as a power of two beside the set: 2^n for n chiral carbons, 2^m for m cis-trans C=C, 2^(m+n) for both, and show the meso reduction arithmetic where relevant (e.g. 'Theoretical 2^2 = 4 / Actual 4 - 1 = 3'). An alternative vertically-stacked form (tartaric acid, NJC answers p6) stacks the two C's on a vertical plain bond with substituents on left/right/wedge/dash arms.

drawing_spec.visual_spec: Draw the multi-stereocentre molecule as a SINGLE structure (not an enantiomer pair) on the same two-carbon flying-wedge template, then overlay an internal PLANE OF SYMMETRY. Two accepted renderings: (a) a VERTICAL DASHED line through the MIDPOINT of the central C-C bond (bisecting the molecule left/right) so the left half reflects onto the right half — same dashed style as the enantiomer mirror line but placed INSIDE one molecule; (b) for a vertically-stacked backbone, a HORIZONTAL dashed line across the middle bond so the top half reflects onto the bottom half. Some sources upgrade this to a small upright 3-D parallelogram/lens drawn edge-on through the central bond. Caption 'plane of symmetry' and note the molecule is achiral / optically inactive despite having stereocentres. CRITICAL disambiguation: a vertical dashed line BETWEEN two separate molecules = an enantiomer mirror plane; a dashed line THROUGH the middle of ONE molecule = an internal meso symmetry plane. Position is the only disambiguator, so always keep the meso line inside the single structure.

drawing_spec.topic: Ring cis/trans with wedge/dash on a polygon
drawing_spec.visual_spec: For cis-trans from restricted rotation in a RING, draw the ring as a plain regular polygon in the plane of the paper (cyclohexane = hexagon, cyclobutane = square, benzene = hexagon with inscribed circle). The two relevant adjacent substituted ring carbons each carry TWO out-of-ring bonds: one BOLD WEDGE (front, toward viewer) and one HASHED DASH (back, away), drawn splaying up-and-out / down-and-out from that vertex; the ring edges themselves are the two in-plane plain bonds. cis = the two reference groups on the SAME face (both on wedges or both on dashes); trans = on OPPOSITE faces (one wedge, one dash for the reference pair). Mark each stereogenic ring vertex with an asterisk (*) placed just inside the polygon. A chiral ring isomer is then shown as its own enantiomer pair (two polygons flanking a vertical dashed mirror line); a meso ring isomer (e.g. cis-cyclobutane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid) is drawn as a single structure with its plane of symmetry. Label 'cis'/'trans' below.
sources: YIJC 17 Isomerism.pdf p4 (1,2-dibromo-1-methylcyclohexane hexagon; cyclobutane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid square)
Ember ISOMERISM TUTORIAL — TEACHER.pdf p5-6 (same two ring systems)

NJC Isomerism Tutorial Answer.pdf (ring C=C cannot be cis-trans note)

drawing_spec.visual_spec: Mark every chiral carbon with an asterisk (*) placed at/just above the carbon (red on flat/condensed formulae in the notes; black is acceptable). On skeletal formulae the * sits at the chain/ring vertex; on condensed 3-D drawings it sits on the letter 'C'. To locate a stereocentre in skeletal form: find a vertex where 3 lines meet (4th bond = implicit C-H) or 4 lines meet, then confirm 4 different groups. HARD labelling rules for A-level H2 (9729/9476): NEVER print CIP R/S descriptors, NEVER print E/Z on a geometric isomer, and do not put D/L or (+)/(-) on the structures themselves (optical rotation is discussed only in prose: dextrorotatory = D or (+), laevorotatory = L or (-)). A C=C inside a ring cannot show cis-trans and must be excluded from any 2^n count.
sources: NJC Isomerism Lecture Notes (Student).pdf p7,p9 (asterisk convention), p1/p6 (E/Z not in syllabus)
Ember EMBER ISOMERISM.pdf notes p9 (red *), p8 (D/L prose only)

drawing_spec.topic: Fischer projection (secondary / not the A-level default)
drawing_spec.visual_spec: Used mainly for polyhydroxy / di-acid chains (tartaric acid) in the NJC/YIJC notes; the web sources flag Fischer as NOT the A-level drawing standard, so gate it behind an explicit option and keep wedge/dash as default. Draw a single VERTICAL straight backbone line with the terminal groups (e.g. CO2H) at top and bottom; each chiral carbon is a CROSS (a horizontal line crossing the vertical) with the carbon AT the intersection, NO letter 'C' and NO wedge/dash. Convention (implicit): horizontal bonds project toward the viewer, vertical bonds project away. Tartaric acid: CO2H top, then two stacked crosses each with H on the left arm and OH on the right arm, then CO2H bottom. When identifying stereocentres, add an explicit 'C' with an asterisk (*) at each crossing.
sources: NJC Isomerism Lecture Notes (Student).pdf p18 (tartaric acid Fischer)
YIJC 17 Isomerism.pdf p5 (tartaric acid vertical displayed formula)
NJC Isomerism Tutorial Answer.pdf p6 (Fischer + red *)
web: LibreTexts (Fischer: vertical=back, horizontal=front) with A-level scope note that wedge/dash is the standard

current_impl_critique.issue: Wedge and dash are drawn HORIZONTAL on opposite sides: _stereo_layout sets wdg=(1.45,0) and dsh=(-1.45,0). Every source explicitly forbids this — NJC p9 states the wedge/dash are '~45 deg off vertical, never horizontal', and the authentic layout puts the wedge and dash on the SAME side (both left or both right), one up-ish and one down-ish. Horizontal, opposite-side wedge/dash is not any documented house style.
current_impl_critique.fix: Replace the four fixed positions with the flying-wedge template: plain UP ~90 deg, plain DOWN-RIGHT ~-55 deg, DASH UP-LEFT ~135 deg, WEDGE DOWN-LEFT ~-125 deg (wedge+dash both on the left). Provide the right-side mirror variant for the second enantiomer.

current_impl_critique.issue: The two plain bonds are collinear at 180 deg: up=(0,1.35) and down=(0,-1.35) draw CH3 and COOH as a straight vertical line through the C. Combined with the horizontal wedge/dash this produces a 90-deg four-way CROSS, which reads as a square-planar / Fischer-cross layout and misrepresents the sp3 tetrahedral centre the wedge/dash are meant to convey.
current_impl_critique.fix: Never place the two plain bonds at 180 deg. In the flying-wedge template the plain bonds go up (~90 deg) and down-to-a-side (~-55 deg), ~120 deg apart, so the four bonds read as a tetrahedral projection.

current_impl_critique.issue: render_stereo_pair draws the two enantiomers with NO vertical mirror-plane line between them and captions them 'one enantiomer' / 'mirror image'. Every source (NJC notes p7, Ember notes p7, YIJC p3, Ember tutorial p10, NJC alkene p12) draws a thin vertical dashed/dotted line in the gap, usually labelled 'mirror plane', with the pair captioned 'enantiomers / non-superimposable mirror images'.
current_impl_critique.fix: In render_stereo_pair, draw a central vertical dashed line between the two structures, add a 'mirror plane' label above it, and change the pair caption to 'enantiomers (non-superimposable mirror images)'.

current_impl_critique.issue: No cis/trans (geometric) isomerism support at all — an entire A-level stereochemistry drawing type is missing. There is no C=C layout, so but-2-ene, 1,2-dichloroethene, dibromoethene etc. cannot be rendered.
current_impl_critique.fix: Add a _geometric_layout(mol) that draws a horizontal explicit C=C (double line) with four plain substituent bonds at ~120 deg, places reference groups same-side (cis) / diagonal (trans), labels 'cis'/'trans' (never E/Z), and refuses to draw when a carbon bears two identical groups.

current_impl_critique.issue: Only the FIRST chiral centre is handled: c = centres[0][0]. Molecules with two or more stereocentres (tartaric acid, the CHBrF-CHBr systems, cyclobutane/cyclohexane dicarboxylic/dibromo cases), the 2^n count, and meso compounds are all unsupported.
current_impl_critique.fix: Add a horizontal two-carbon flying-wedge backbone layout (H up plain on each C, one dash + one wedge below each), support enantiomer-pair and 2x2 grid output, annotate 2^n, and add meso detection with an internal plane-of-symmetry line.

current_impl_critique.issue: The drawing is configuration-blind: wedge/dash are assigned purely by neighbour ordering (carbons+hetero+hydro)[:4] — heteroatom always goes on the wedge-right, H always on the dash-left — so the drawn 3-D configuration ignores the @/@@ parity in the SMILES. The renderer cannot draw a SPECIFIED enantiomer, and the 'mirror' is just a reflection of an arbitrary guess.
current_impl_critique.fix: Read the RDKit CIP parity / atom chiral tag at the stereocentre and choose which lower group is wedge vs dash so the drawn arrangement matches the SMILES; generate the partner by a single true inversion (reflect x OR swap wedge<->dash, not both).

current_impl_critique.issue: No asterisk (*) marks the chiral carbon, and there is no guard against emitting R/S or E/Z. The 9729 house convention flags each stereocentre with a *, and R/S, E/Z, D/L and (+)/(-) must never appear on the structures.
current_impl_critique.fix: Add an optional superscript '*' next to each stereocentre, and keep the label pipeline free of R/S, E/Z, D/L and +/- text so the output stays in-syllabus.

current_impl_critique.issue: All six example molecules render as an identical template (heteroatom on wedge-right, H on dash-left, chain vertical) — the 'naive' tell. Authentic notes vary the layout per molecule (e.g. lactic acid in the source draws OH on an up-right dash and CO2H on a down-right wedge with CH3 up and H down-left).
current_impl_critique.fix: Once the flying-wedge template and configuration-aware assignment are in, per-molecule variation follows naturally; expose the left/right handedness so worked examples can match their source figures.

rebuild_plan.step: Rewrite _stereo_layout to use the flying-wedge tetrahedral template instead of the 90-deg cross
rebuild_plan.detail: Replace positions up=(0,1.35),down=(0,-1.35),wdg=(1.45,0),dsh=(-1.45,0) with an angle-based template: plain UP ~90 deg, plain DOWN-RIGHT ~-55 deg, DASH UP-LEFT ~135 deg, WEDGE DOWN-LEFT ~-125 deg (wedge+dash on the same side, ~120 deg spacing). Parameterise a 'handedness' flag to emit the right-side mirror variant. Keep the explicit letter 'C' at the centre and condensed group labels. Assert per centre exactly 2 plain + 1 wedge + 1 dash, and that neither wedge nor dash is horizontal.

rebuild_plan.step: Make wedge/dash assignment configuration-aware from the SMILES parity
rebuild_plan.detail: At the stereocentre, read the RDKit chiral tag / CIP code and decide which of the two non-plain groups is the wedge and which the dash so the drawn 3-D matches the input configuration. Document the mapping. Generate the enantiomer by a SINGLE inversion (reflect x of the corrected template, or swap wedge<->dash), never both.

rebuild_plan.step: Add the vertical mirror-plane line and correct captions to render_stereo_pair
rebuild_plan.detail: After tiling the two enantiomers, draw a thin vertical dashed line centred in the gap, add a 'mirror plane' label above it, and caption the pair 'enantiomers (non-superimposable mirror images)'. Keep the tile helper but special-case the 2-up enantiomer pair so the dashed line lands exactly between the structures.

rebuild_plan.step: Implement _geometric_layout for cis/trans across a C=C
rebuild_plan.detail: Detect the stereogenic double bond (RDKit bond stereo, or accept explicit cis/trans SMILES). Draw a horizontal C=C as two explicit 'C' letters with a double line; place four plain substituent bonds at ~120 deg into up-left/down-left/up-right/down-right slots. Put the two reference groups same-side for cis, diagonal for trans; label 'cis'/'trans' below (name-prefix option too). Raise a clear error if either alkene carbon has two identical substituents. Never emit E/Z.

rebuild_plan.step: Add multi-stereocentre acyclic backbone layout + 2^n annotation
rebuild_plan.detail: Draw a horizontal C-C (or vertical-stacked) backbone of letter 'C's; on each carbon put H up on a plain bond and the other two groups below as one outward dash + one downward wedge. Support enantiomer-pair output (double-headed 'Enantiomers' arrow or dashed mirror line) and a 2x2 A/B/C/D grid. Print the maximum-count arithmetic (2^n, 2^m, 2^(m+n), and the meso reduction e.g. 4-1=3).

rebuild_plan.step: Add meso detection and the internal plane-of-symmetry line
rebuild_plan.detail: Detect meso (RDKit: has stereocentres but achiral / internal mirror). Render as a SINGLE structure with a dashed plane through the mid C-C bond (vertical for a horizontal backbone, horizontal for a stacked backbone), labelled 'plane of symmetry'. Ensure this line is drawn INSIDE the molecule, distinct from the between-molecules enantiomer mirror line.

rebuild_plan.step: Add ring cis/trans (polygon + wedge/dash on two adjacent vertices)
rebuild_plan.detail: Reuse the existing _ring_layout polygon; for the two adjacent substituted ring carbons, add one bold wedge + one hashed dash splaying out of the ring per carbon, mark each stereogenic vertex with '*', place reference groups same-face (cis) / opposite-face (trans), and route chiral ring isomers through the enantiomer-pair path and meso ring isomers through the single-structure plane-of-symmetry path.

rebuild_plan.step: Add asterisk marking and enforce the no-R/S / no-E/Z labelling policy
rebuild_plan.detail: Add an optional superscript '*' near each stereocentre (letter C or skeletal vertex). Add a guard/lint in the label pipeline that never emits R, S, E, Z, D, L or +/- descriptors on a structure, keeping output within 9729/9476 scope.

rebuild_plan.step: Add an optional (non-default) Fischer projection mode
rebuild_plan.detail: For tartaric-acid-type polyhydroxy/di-acid chains, offer a Fischer option: vertical backbone line, terminal groups top/bottom, each stereocentre a horizontal cross with no letter C and no wedge/dash (horizontal=front, vertical=back). Keep wedge/dash as the default per the web scope note; add explicit 'C'+'*' at crossings when identifying centres.

rebuild_plan.step: Add stereo invariants/tests and visual verification
rebuild_plan.detail: Extend tests/invariants.py: assert every stereocentre has exactly 2 plain + 1 wedge + 1 dash; assert neither wedge nor dash is horizontal and the two plain bonds are not collinear; assert the enantiomer pair contains a vertical dashed mirror line; assert cis places reference groups same-side and trans diagonal; assert no R/S or E/Z text is emitted. Re-render butan-2-ol, but-2-ene, tartaric acid and eyeball against the source figures.

worked_examples.stereo_type: optical isomerism, single chiral centre, enantiomer pair with mirror plane
worked_examples.target_drawing: Two flying-wedge structures side by side split by a vertical dashed 'mirror plane' line, captioned 'enantiomers (non-superimposable mirror images)'. LEFT: letter 'C' centre; CH2CH3 plain UP ~90 deg; CH3 plain DOWN-RIGHT ~-55 deg; H on a HASHED DASH UP-LEFT ~135 deg; HO on a BOLD WEDGE DOWN-LEFT ~-125 deg (wedge+dash both on the left). RIGHT = exact reflection: CH2CH3 up; CH3 plain down-left; H dash UP-RIGHT; OH wedge DOWN-RIGHT. No R/S, no +/-.

worked_examples.stereo_type: optical isomerism, single chiral centre, enantiomer pair
worked_examples.target_drawing: Letter 'C' centre; CH2CH3 plain UP; CH3 plain DOWN to a side; H on a BOLD WEDGE; Br on a HASHED DASH to the side (per NJC alkene p12). Two structures flank a vertical dashed line labelled 'mirror plane' above and 'enantiomers' below; the Br-dash and CH3 swap sides between the two while CH2CH3(up) and H(wedge) reflect into corresponding positions. No R/S/+/- labels.

One flying-wedge structure (bare vertex or explicit C): CH3 plain UP; H plain DOWN-LEFT; OH on a HASHED DASH UP-RIGHT (into plane); CO2H on a BOLD WEDGE DOWN-RIGHT (out of plane) — wedge+dash open to the RIGHT, forming a narrow V, per NJC Intro-Organic p5. For a pair, add the reflected partner across a vertical dashed mirror line. Carboxyl written 'CO2H'. No R/S.

Horizontal C=C (two letter 'C' with a double line). cis: CH3 up-left AND CH3 up-right (both top, same side), H down-left and H down-right; label 'cis' below. trans: CH3 up-left and H up-right, H down-left and CH3 down-right (methyls diagonal); label 'trans' below. All four substituent bonds plain at ~120 deg; no wedge/dash; no E/Z.

Horizontal C=C. cis-1,2-dichloroethene: Cl up-left AND Cl up-right (both top), H bottom-left and H bottom-right — optionally two down-pointing dipole arrows + resultant, 'polar molecule'. trans: Cl up-left, H up-right, H down-left, Cl down-right (Cl diagonal) — opposed cancelling dipoles, 'non-polar molecule'. Italic 'cis'/'trans' labels; never E/Z.

worked_examples.stereo_type: two stereocentres: enantiomer pair (A/B) + one meso form (C); 2^2=4 but only 3 distinct
worked_examples.target_drawing: Molecules A and B: two-carbon flying-wedge backbone (two 'C', each *), drawn as non-superimposable mirror images across a vertical dashed mirror line (invert BOTH centres). Molecule C (meso): a SINGLE structure with CO2H/CO2H, OH's and H's arranged symmetrically and an internal 'plane of symmetry' drawn as a dashed line (or edge-on parallelogram) bisecting the central C-C bond; captioned achiral / optically inactive. Annotate 'Theoretical 2^2 = 4 / Actual = 3'. No R/S.

worked_examples.stereo_type: ring cis/trans; trans = enantiomer pair, cis = meso
worked_examples.target_drawing: Ring drawn as a plain SQUARE; the two bottom corners are the stereocentres (each *). Each corner: one substituent on a BOLD WEDGE up-and-out, one on a HASHED DASH down-and-out. cis (both COOH on dashes = same face): single structure with an internal plane of symmetry = meso, achiral. trans (COOH on opposite faces): chiral, redrawn as an enantiomer pair (two squares flanking a vertical dashed mirror line). 'cis'/'trans' labelled below.

worked_examples.molecule: Bromochlorofluoromethane (edge case: four heteroatom/H groups, no carbon neighbours)
worked_examples.stereo_type: optical isomerism, single chiral centre (four different atoms directly on C)
worked_examples.target_drawing: Flying-wedge on the letter 'C': two of {F, Cl} on the plain bonds (e.g. F plain UP, Cl plain DOWN-RIGHT), H on a HASHED DASH UP-LEFT, Br on a BOLD WEDGE DOWN-LEFT — wedge+dash on the same side, ~120 deg spacing (NOT the collinear-vertical + horizontal cross the current code produces). Enantiomer = reflected partner across a vertical dashed mirror line.
